response.title: Harborlight FY2026 Results and a Sixth Site

segments.heading: The big picture
segments.text: Harborlight served more adult learners than ever in fiscal year 2026. Now staff want to grow again. They recommend an FY2027 budget of $1,610,000. The budget adds a sixth site at the Eastgate branch library. It also adds two site coordinators. Staff estimate the new site would serve 180 more learners a year. They also estimate it would cut the waitlist in half.

segments.heading: Who came to learn
segments.text: Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners in fiscal year 2026. The year before, it enrolled 936. Learners came to five neighborhood sites. Of them, 412 were working toward a high school equivalency credential. And 389 were English language learners. The results were strong. Sixty-eight percent of learners who stayed at least 12 weeks gained one or more reading levels on the CASAS assessment. Seventy-one learners earned a high school equivalency credential. No year in the organization's history has been higher.

segments.heading: The people doing the work
segments.text: Volunteers do much of the work. A corps of 214 volunteer tutors gave 9,870 tutoring hours. On average, a tutor stayed 14 months. Harborlight also has 11 full-time staff. Four of them are site coordinators. A learner at the Riverside site summed up what this work means. Quote. I read my granddaughter a bedtime story for the first time this spring. End quote.

segments.heading: Where the money went
segments.text: Operating expenses for FY2026 came to $1,420,000. Program costs made up 81 percent of spending. Foundation grants brought in $640,000. Individual donors gave $388,000. The city's adult education contract paid $295,000. Each learner cost $1,237 to serve. There is one caution. Treasurer Dev Patel reported that reserves stand at 3.2 months of operating expenses. The board's target is 4 months. That leaves reserves below target.

segments.heading: Adults still waiting
segments.text: More adults want to learn than Harborlight has room for. At year end, 287 adults sat on the waitlist. Most of them were at the Eastgate and Riverside sites. They waited nine weeks on average. The proposed sixth site would sit at the Eastgate branch library. Eastgate is one of the two sites where most of the waiting adults are.

segments.heading: What the board wants
segments.text: The board made two requests at its September 13 retreat. First, it asked staff for a one-page summary of the FY2027 budget request. Staff should bring it to the October 21 board meeting. Second, board members want a short deck to use with funders when they talk about the sixth site. The board also agreed to vote on the FY2027 budget on October 21.

response.recap: Three things to remember. First, Harborlight enrolled 1,148 adult learners, and seventy-one earned a high school equivalency credential, a record. Second, 287 adults were on the waitlist, and the average wait was nine weeks. Third, staff recommend a $1,610,000 FY2027 budget that adds a sixth site, while reserves stand at 3.2 months, short of the 4-month target.
